raw_answer_text:
A1: DHCPDISCOVER, DHCPOFFER, DHCPREQUEST, DHCPACK, in that order, with the client broadcasting the first message (DHCPDISCOVER).
A2: A server sends both the DHCPOFFER and the DHCPACK.
A3: The DHCPACK message moves the client into the BOUND state.
A4: The client moves into the RENEWING state and sends the DHCPREQUEST unicast directly to the server that granted the original lease.
A5: The client moves into the REBINDING state and broadcasts the DHCPREQUEST to all servers rather than unicasting it to the original server.
A6: Yes, the client continues to use its existing address while renewing/rebinding; if the lease expires with no DHCPACK received, it must stop using the address and return to the INIT state to acquire a new one.
A7: A DHCPRELEASE message tells the server the client is voluntarily giving up the address and terminating the lease early; it is sent by the client.
A8: The client broadcasts a DHCPREQUEST that identifies (via the server identifier option) the specific server/offer it has accepted; servers whose offers were not selected see this and conclude their offers were declined, freeing the offered addresses.
